summary_of_core_decisions: The text's core move is to separate the logical (semantic) plane from the ontological (existential) plane. It validates Englebretsen's critique of Gyekye's equivocation, but then identifies a residual problem: even if the semantic/ontological distinction is maintained, Aristotle's ontological reductionism (only substances exist) still clashes with the requirement that scientific knowledge (episteme) is of universals. The text ends by posing this as an open question, thereby shifting the dialectic from a resolved local dispute to an unresolved global tension in Aristotelian metaphysics.
